Project: [RPT-P1] HSA-1240: 12-bit SAR ADC + LDO sensor front-end ## Project Vision & Context **Project Name:** HSA-1240: 12-bit SAR ADC + LDO Sensor Front-End **Client:** Halvorsen Analog **Process Node:** 180 nm-class 5 V CMOS The HSA-1240 is a critical low-power, integrated sensor front-end IP block designed for Halvorsen Analog’s industrial pressure-sensor product line. The core vision is to deliver a robust, high-performance analog subsystem that combines high-resolution data conversion with stable on-chip power delivery within a minimal footprint. This IP block is intended to meet stringent industrial reliability standards, ensuring high accuracy and low power consumption in harsh operating environments (industrial temperature range of -40°C to 125°C). ## Technical Scope The project scope is strictly limited to the **Analog IP Design**, comprising three tightly coupled sub-blocks: 1. **12-bit SAR ADC**: * **Performance:** 1 MS/s conversion rate, ENOB >= 11.0 bits, INL/DNL within +/-1 LSB. * **Input:** Differential, 0-3.3 V range. * **Power:** <= 1.5 mW at 1 MS/s. 2. **On-chip LDO (Low Dropout Regulator)**: * **Specifications:** 5 V input, 3.3 V output, 50 mA load capability. * **Performance:** Dropout <= 250 mV, PSRR >= 50 dB at 1 kHz. * **Stability:** Must remain stable with output capacitors ranging from 1 µF to 10 µF. 3. **Bandgap Reference (Shared Block)**: * **Function:** Provides the reference voltage for both the ADC and LDO. * **Precision:** Temperature coefficient <= 30 ppm/°C over the full industrial range (-40°C to 125°C). ## Governance & Execution Strategy The project adheres to Halvorsen Analog’s rigorous analog design review process, characterized by: * **Schematic-First Approach:** No block proceeds to layout until schematic and pre-layout simulations are reviewed and approved by a senior designer. * **Simulation Rigor:** All simulation results must explicitly define Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) corners. * **Compliance Tracking:** Strict documentation of spec value, simulated value, and margin for every parameter. * **Sign-off Authority:** Final DRC, LVS, and tape-out readiness are exclusively approved by the **Analog Design Director**. Instructions:

Follow our analog design review process: no block moves to layout before its schematic and pre-layout simulations are reviewed by a senior designer. Every result must state the corner, temperature and supply it was simulated at. Sign-off (DRC, LVS, tape-out readiness) is approved only by the Analog Design Director. Track spec compliance per parameter (spec value, simulated value, margin).

Epic: Bandgap Reference Schematic Design & Pre-Layout Simulation This epic focuses on the design and verification of the shared Bandgap Reference (BGR). The BGR provides the critical voltage reference for both the SAR ADC and LDO. The primary goal is to achieve a temperature coefficient (TC) of <= 30 ppm/°C across the industrial temperature range of -40°C to 125°C. The design must ensure reliable start-up and robust noise performance. Following the 'Schematic-First' approach, the schematic and comprehensive temperature sweep simulations must be reviewed and signed off by the Senior Analog Designer before layout. Expectations: A validated BGR schematic and temperature coefficient simulation report, signed off by the Senior Analog Designer. Story: Bandgap Reference Schematic Design & Nominal Verification Design and verify the core Bandgap Reference (BGR) schematic targeting a temperature coefficient (TC) of <= 30 ppm/°C. This story covers the selection of a robust topology (e.g., Brokaw cell with fractional Bandgap architecture for high linearity), the design of the start-up circuit to prevent latching in low-sensitivity operating points, and the creation of the transistor-level netlist. The design must be simulated at nominal conditions (TT corner, 25°C, 5.0V supply) to establish a baseline operating point and confirm the theoretical linearity/TC limits. This establishes the foundation for subsequent PVT verification. The deliverable is a version-controlled Xschem schematic and netlist, validated for DC operating point integrity and start-up reliability. ### Review feedback to address - Revision requested by review: Rejected at senior review. This is not a working bandgap: M6/M7 have drain=source=VDD, N5 floats, there is no PTAT/CTAT loop and VREF is unloaded. A bandgap needs bipolar transistors (or diodes) and resistors. Also no simulation was actually run, yet the report says the simulation steps are done. Redo the core with a proper Brokaw or Kuijk topology, then run DC operating point and a temperature sweep -40 to 125 C at TT and report VREF and the TC in ppm/C. - Revision requested by review: Second senior review: the bandgap is still not a working circuit (no PTAT/CTAT loop, shorted PMOS, floating N5) and nothing was simulated. Redo bgr_core as a real bandgap and run a DC operating point plus a -40 to 125 C temperature sweep at TT; report VREF and the TC in ppm/C. If the platform cannot represent resistors or bipolars, say so plainly instead of removing them.

plan.title: Bandgap Reference Schematic Design & Nominal Verification - Simulation Rework
plan.summary: Re-run all required simulations for the bandgap reference (bgr_core, bgr_startup, bgr_top) to address senior review feedback. Perform DC operating point and startup transient simulations at TT/25C/5V. Report Vref and startup time. Clearly state if resistors or bipolars cannot be represented in the platform.
